newsitem.title: USA: Barrick Gold sees solid output growth.
newsitem.headline: Barrick Gold sees solid output growth.

text.p: Barrick Gold Corp expects its gold output rise to rise to four million ounces or more by the year 2000 with the addition of reserves from its Pascua Mine in Chile and the Pierina property in Peru, a senior executive said on Wednesday.
Barrick acquired Pierina when it took over exploration company Arequipa Resources Ltd, an acquisition it finalized at the end of August, for C$1 billion.
"Today Barrick produces 3.2 million ounces a year, the third-highest in the world," said Alan Hill, Barrick executive vice-president, in a speech prepared for the Denver Gold Show.
"In less than four years' time, Pascua and Pierina mines will jointly add between 80,000 and 900,000 ounces to our total," Hill added.

He said that investors can expect Barrick to announce a solid rise in its reserves at the end of the year as well as, for the first time, resource numbers. Barrick said that while revealing resource numbers has not been its custom in the past, it has become an industry practice.
